comments.quote_zh: 关于 City of London 和那个叫 London 的城市有何不同，可以看 CGP Grey 的那个精彩视频[1]
comments.text_zh: 简短的回答是“不”。长一点的回答是“嗯，算是吧，但也不尽然”。确实有过几起定罪，但都是认罪——这些人要么是被自己的律师误导了（很可能因为律师不是版权法专家），要么就是实在不想走完整个审判程序。版权行业曾试图完全绕开版权法，改用法律依据极其可疑的“共谋欺诈”罪名。不过这种情况远谈不上常见。被起诉的尝试只有寥寥几起，而且通常只是因为版权行业（通过 FACT[0]）向警方施压。最近他们还腐̶蚀̶了——呃，是拉拢了伦敦金融城警察局。这支警力负责的正是伦敦市中心那一平方英里的伦敦金融城（关于 City of London 和那个叫 London 的城市有何不同，可以看 CGP Grey 的那个精彩视频[1]）。[0] “反版权盗窃联合会”（Federation Against Copyright Theft）——一个荒谬组织起的荒谬名字——[LINK] [1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: The short answer is "no". The longer answer is "well, kinda, but not really". There have been a couple of convictions, but these were guilty pleas - people who have either been advised incorrectly by their solicitors (most probably because they were not experts in copyright law) or just really did not want to go through a trial. The copyright industry has tried to completely side-step copyright law entirely and use the offence of "conspiracy to defraud" with very dubious legal basis. It's been far from common, though. There have only been a handful of attempted prosecutions, and usually only because the copyright industry (via FACT[0]) has leant on the police. Most recently they've c̶o̶r̶r̶u̶p̶t̶e̶d̶ err, co-opted the City of London Police. This is the force that polices the square-mile City of London in the heart of London (See CGP Grey's excellent video[1] for more about the City of London vs the city called London). [0] The 'Federation Against Copyright Theft' - an absurd name for an absurd organisation - [LINK] [1] [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: 我觉得你的评论有点危言耸听，而且缺少历史背景。City of London（Garden Bridge 靠 Temple 那一端就始于这里）比英国本身还要古老好几百上千年，一直以来都是私人所有，由隐秘的、公司化的、神秘的流程治理。传统上，就连女王未经 Lord Mayor 许可也不能进入 City of London。这个“以公共空间形式运作的私人地方”已经运转了好几个世纪，并主导了伦敦崛起为全球领先金融中心的过程，直到不久前伦敦还是世界上有史以来最大帝国的首都。我承认，就市中心公共空间的私有制讨论其利弊是合理的，但我的意思是：在这个案例里，City of London 既有历史独特性又很重要，而且从很多方面衡量，它对其所属国家都是巨大的成功。关于这个话题有一个既有信息量又有趣的视频：[VIDEO]
comments.text: I find your comment somewhat alarmist, and lacking historical context. The City of London (from which the Temple end of the Garden Bridge starts) is many many hundreds of years older than the UK itself, and has always been privately owned and governed by shadowy, corporate and arcane processes. Traditionally even the Queen is not allowed to enter the City of London without the say-so of the Lord Mayor. This "private place operating as a public space" has been operating for centuries and stewarded the emergence of London as a leading global financial centre and until recently capital of the largest Empire the world has ever seen. I admit it's reasonable to debate the pros and cons of private ownership of public spaces in city centres, but my point is that in this case The City of London is both historically unique and important, and by many measures been a huge success for the host nation. Informative/fun video on the subject: [VIDEO]

comments.text: I don’t know whether this is true because I never looked into it really, but a colleague of mine in the ndustry told me I could join the banker’s guild. His words were that because I lived in the city[1] at the time, and also worked for a bank in the city, I’d be eligible for membership if the bank would nominate or sponsor me as a representative. I’m hazy on the details, it was years ago, and I don’t really know whether it’s true since as mentioned I never checked it out. I kind of regret not doing so now though, since moving out of the city I’ve learned much more of it’s (weird and interesting) history and it would’ve been fun to at least try to see some of this from the inside. It probably wouldn’t have worked anyway, but would’ve been fun to try. For anyone looking for a fun little intro to the weirdness of the city and it’s history, I recommend CGP Grey’s channel and particularly his videos on the City of London[2][3]. [1]: for the benefit of people who might not be aware – “the city” is a colloquialism for the City of London, which is a small somewhat autonomous part of London, situated east of what most people (who don’t know this) probably think of when you say the city of London. comments.text_zh: > City of London 并不比 NYC 更奇怪……真的，不奇怪？跟什么比？梵蒂冈？它可以说是世界的金融（离岸）之都，住着超过一万一千人。City of London 位于名为 London 的城市内部，但这两个 London 有各自的市政厅，选举各自的市长，征收各自的税，资助各自的警察，执行各自的法律。City of London 的市长被称为“The Right Honourable Lord Mayor of London”，以匹配他那身花哨的行头。他可以乘坐金色马车，在 Guildhall 办公，而 London 市长则得穿西装、骑自行车、在办公楼里办公。City of London 还有自己的旗帜和自己的徽章，行事更像 UK 里的一个国家，而不只是一个位置古怪的城市。管理 City of London 的那个 corporation 比 United Kingdom 还早几百年。它由罗马人在公元 43 年创建，名为“Londonimium”，配有他们的神庙、公共浴场、道路、桥梁，以及一堵用来保卫其工程的墙。正是这堵墙解释了现今 City of London 为何存在——因为尽管罗马人来来去去，王国兴衰更替，这堵墙始终屹立，保护着墙内的城市。罗马人之后，William the Conqueror 来到 Great Britain，开启现代英国历史；他发现 City of London 拥有坚固的城墙，比开阔田野上的农民更难击败。于是他同意承认 Cit 的权利和特权
comments.text: > City of London is no weirder than NYC ... really, not weird? compared to what? the Vatican? It's arguably the financial (offshore) capital of the world and home to over eleven thousand people. The City of London lives inside of the city named London but the two Londons have separate city halls and elect separate mayors, who collect separate taxes to fund separate police who enforce separate laws. The Mayor of the City of London is called 'The Right Honourable Lord Mayor of London' to match his fancy outfit. He gets to ride in a golden carriage and work in a Guildhall while the mayor of London has to wear a suit, ride a bike and work in an office building. The City of London also has its own flag and its own crest and gets to act more like one of the countries in the UK than just an oddly located city. The corporation that runs the city of London is older than the United Kingdom by several hundred years. It was created by Romans in 43 CE as "Londonimium" with their temples, public baths, roads, bridges and a wall to defend their work. It's this wall which is why the current City of London exists - for though the Romans came and the Romans went and kingdoms rose and kingdoms fell, the wall endured protecting the city within. After the Romans William the Conqueror came to Great Britain to begin modern British history he found the City of London, with its sturdy walls more challenging to defeat than farmers on open fields.
